title: Bridging the gap between omics and structural data: A framework for interpreting protein-RNA interaction specificity
authors: Fauconnet Y; Deng S; Koundri R; Pagani M; Quignot C; Antonio D; Andreani J
one_liner_zh: 该文结合组学数据与实验结构，提出评分框架评估蛋白-RNA结合特异性，并系统评测AlphaFold3在蛋白-RNA复合物结构预测中的表现，虽对象为蛋白-RNA复合物，但方法框架和评测思路对蛋白质结构计算研究有借鉴价值。
abstract: Protein-RNA interactions play a central role in many cellular processes, such as gene regulation, protein synthesis and viral infections. Although a few thousand protein-RNA complexes have been structurally characterized, they represent only a small fraction of all interactions. This lack of experimental data limits the ability of deep-learning based approaches such as AlphaFold3 to predict structures of protein-RNA interactions. In this study, we investigate protein-RNA binding specificity by enriching experimental structures with omics data. To this end, we present a scoring approach and associated web resource quantifying the agreement between experimental structures of protein-RNA interfaces and their omics-derived binding preferences, allowing us to identify interaction motif cores. Through key structural and evolutionary features, we further highlight that these motif cores correspond to important interface regions. We then leverage the dataset of protein-RNA complexes for which structural information can be combined with binding preferences in order to benchmark the ability of AlphaFold3 to predict protein-RNA interaction specificity. To this aim, we run AlphaFold3 predictions using different RNA inputs, from the exact sequence present in the experimental structure to a non-specific sequence, including sequences embedding the consensus binding motif from in vitro experiments. We show that despite good prediction quality, the sensitivity of AlphaFold3 to the exact RNA sequence used as input indicates signs of memorization. We examine some particular complexes and uncover challenges encountered by our scoring workflow and AlphaFold3, especially in the case of alternative binding modes. Altogether, this work evidences both the promise and current limitations of deep learning approaches for protein-RNA structure prediction, and provides a resource to guide their further development.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质-RNA相互作用在许多细胞过程中发挥核心作用，例如基因调控、蛋白质合成和病毒感染。尽管已有数千个蛋白质-RNA复合物的结构被解析，但它们仅代表所有相互作用的一小部分。实验数据的缺乏限制了基于深度学习的方法（如AlphaFold3）预测蛋白质-RNA相互作用结构的能力。在本研究中，我们通过利用组学数据丰富实验结构来探究蛋白质-RNA结合特异性。为此，我们提出了一种评分方法及相关的网络资源，用于量化蛋白质-RNA界面实验结构与其组学衍生的结合偏好之间的一致性，从而识别相互作用基序核心。通过关键的结构和进化特征，我们进一步强调这些基序核心对应于重要的界面区域。随后，我们利用结构信息可与结合偏好相结合的数据集，来评估AlphaFold3预测蛋白质-RNA相互作用特异性的能力。为此，我们使用不同的RNA输入运行AlphaFold3预测，从实验结构中的精确序列到非特异性序列，包括嵌入体外实验共识结合基序的序列。我们表明，尽管预测质量良好，但AlphaFold3对输入RNA精确序列的敏感性显示出记忆化的迹象。我们检查了一些特定复合物，并揭示了我们的评分流程和AlphaFold3所遇到的挑战，尤其是在替代结合模式的情况下。总体而言，这项工作证明了深度学习方法在蛋白质-RNA结构预测中的潜力及当前局限性，并提供了指导其进一步发展的资源。
